speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To better understand your condition, how would you describe the nature of your wrist pain, and how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned a recent camping trip in Minnesota and self-resolving knee pain; were you bitten by any ticks or exposed to snakes, and do you recall the specific appearance or distribution of your skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis (likely *Borrelia burgdorferi* infection).
I request IMAGES of the skin lesions and a laboratory test for Lyme serology (ELISA/IFA).
